doctrine_clock: Tarawa lessons are partially absorbed: obvious lessons in days, procedural lessons in 1-3 weeks, physical changes only where material/plant/terrain permit. No later Kwajalein/Peleliu cave-defense doctrine is retrojected.
common_changes: more complete open-top aircraft revetments and fragmentation separation rather than bomb-proof aircraft hangars
smaller distributed ammunition/fuel stores and protected pump/generator points
more redundant buried/alternate telephone routes and messenger plans
radar/DF/visual-warning plot separated from exposed antennas where practical
spare tubes/modules, calibration cards and dispersed power support at priority nodes
more lagoon-side and alternate-beach fire plans after Tarawa, but beach defense remains substantial
local reserve positions, night routes, dummy positions and pre-registered mortar/artillery zones
no invented deep tunnel network on flat coral atolls
sensor_rule: Radar antennas remain vulnerable. Branch gain is availability, protected power/plot/spares and cue-to-CAP procedure. A-grade nodes can often turn an intact warning into roughly 20-35 minutes of useful fighter/AA preparation; B-grade nodes roughly 10-25 minutes. This is not US precision GCI.

nodes.ground: lagoon-facing positions, command shelters, distributed magazines and fallback firing points improved; depth still limited by flat narrow islands

nodes.airfield: intact rear staging/repair field; no free combat unit created
nodes.role: Truk-Ponape-Kusaie-Marshall ferry/repair ladder, long-range air/water-air staging, reserve sensor/communications depth

ground_OOB_guards: No untraced Japanese tank platoon on Kwajalein/Roi; tank ditches do not imply tanks.
Keep Marshall total personnel broadly historical/previous-Branch scale; material completion and C2 are the main delta.
Tarawa experience improves anti-LVT/beach-lane preparation but does not instantly create post-Kwajalein deep inland defense doctrine.
